questions.question: In Darley and Latané's bystander effect experiment, what was the independent variable?

answers.text: The number of witnesses participants believed were present
Whether participants helped the victim
The severity of the emergency situation
The gender of the participants

questions.question: What is the primary reason experiments are considered high in internal validity?

answers.text: They manipulate the independent variable and control extraneous variables
They use large sample sizes from diverse populations
They are conducted in natural settings rather than laboratories
They always use random sampling from the general population

questions.question: A confounding variable is best defined as:

answers.text: An extraneous variable that varies systematically with the independent variable
Any variable that is difficult to measure accurately
The dependent variable when it produces unexpected results
A variable that the researcher intentionally manipulates

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a placebo control condition?

answers.text: To control for participant expectations of improvement
To reduce the cost of conducting the experiment
To ensure all participants receive some form of treatment
To increase the external validity of the study

questions.question: In a between-subjects experiment, each participant:

answers.text: Is tested in only one condition
Is tested in all conditions of the experiment
Serves as their own control
Must be matched with another participant

questions.question: What is the primary difference between random assignment and random sampling?

answers.text: Random assignment assigns participants to conditions; random sampling selects participants from a population
Random assignment is used in correlational studies; random sampling is used in experiments
Random assignment increases external validity; random sampling increases internal validity
Random assignment is done before data collection; random sampling is done after

questions.question: In Darley and Latané's experiment, what percentage of participants helped when they believed they were the only witness?
A practice effect is an example of what type of problem in within-subjects designs?

answers.text: A carryover effect
A confounding variable
An experimenter expectancy effect
A manipulation check failure

questions.question: What is counterbalancing designed to control in within-subjects experiments?

answers.text: Order effects resulting from the sequence of conditions
Participant dropout rates across conditions
Differences in sample size between groups
Experimenter bias in recording data

questions.question: According to the chapter, what does construct validity assess?

answers.text: How well the experiment's manipulations operationalize the research question
Whether the results can be generalized to other populations
Whether the independent variable caused changes in the dependent variable
The proper use of statistical tests on the data

questions.question: A study that includes one independent variable manipulated to produce three conditions is called a:

answers.text: Single factor multi-level design
Single factor two-level design
Multiple factor design
Factorial design

questions.question: External validity is highest when:

answers.text: The participants and situation studied are similar to those the researcher wants to generalize to
The independent variable is successfully manipulated
All extraneous variables are held constant
The study uses a large number of conditions

questions.question: In block randomization, conditions are arranged so that:

answers.text: All conditions occur once before any is repeated
Each condition appears an equal number of times at each ordinal position
Participants are matched on the dependent variable before assignment
The most important conditions are tested first

questions.question: An experimenter expectancy effect occurs when:

answers.text: The experimenter's expectations about participant behavior unintentionally influence the results
Participants try to behave in ways they think the experimenter wants
The experimental manipulation fails to produce the expected effect
Extraneous variables are not properly controlled

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a manipulation check?

answers.text: To confirm that the independent variable was successfully manipulated
To ensure participants understood the instructions
To measure the dependent variable more accurately
To verify that random assignment was effective

questions.question: In a double-blind study:

answers.text: Neither the participants nor the experimenter knows which condition participants are in
Only the participants are unaware of the research hypothesis
Two different experimenters independently collect the data
The study is replicated twice to confirm results

questions.question: A Latin square design is used in counterbalancing to:

answers.text: Ensure each condition appears at each position and follows each other condition once
Randomly assign participants to experimental conditions
Match participants across conditions on key variables
Eliminate the need for a control group

questions.question: According to the chapter, which of the following is a characteristic of volunteers in psychological research compared to non-volunteers?

answers.text: They are more interested in the research topic
They are less educated on average
They have lower IQs on average
They are less sociable

questions.question: Statistical validity concerns:

answers.text: The proper statistical treatment of data and soundness of statistical conclusions
Whether the results generalize to other populations
The quality of the experimental manipulations
Whether causal conclusions are supported

questions.question: The primary purpose of conducting a pilot test is to:

answers.text: Make sure a new procedure works as planned before conducting the full study
Collect preliminary data to include in the final analysis
Test whether the hypothesis is correct
Determine the appropriate sample size for the main study
